nodes.rationale: Documentation review sets a lower bar per change so that more changes happen: reviewers approve quickly, suggest alternatives and start their own follow-ups for substantial changes, and authors capitulate early instead of arguing.

nodes.rationale: Link other Markdown pages by explicit path rather than a fully qualified URL; relative paths are safe within the same directory, but ../ paths into other directories should be avoided.

nodes.label: Informative link titles
nodes.rationale: Readers scan rather than read, and link text such as 'here', 'link' or a bare URL tells them nothing; write the sentence naturally, then wrap its most descriptive phrase.

nodes.label: Astra agent loop
nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Send the instruction, screenshot history and step budget; execute the actions through EditorSession.act; screenshot and repeat. A step cap, a spend cap, model-produced narration and an explicit reasoning effort are not optional.

nodes.label: Per-run cost estimate ($3.50 with caching, $14.50 without)
nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.norm_label: per-run cost estimate ($3.50 with caching, $14.50 without)
nodes.rationale: The loop resends a growing screenshot history, so cost is quadratic in steps: forty steps send about 1.3M input tokens cumulatively, about $13 uncached against about $2 cached, plus about $1.50 of output.

nodes.label: 272K-token long-request pricing tier
nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Not a risk: the 2x surcharge applies per request, forty frames come to about 63K tokens, and the step cap keeps it that way; exposure is cumulative, not per request.

nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.norm_label: four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Step and spend caps are enforced in the agent loop, free runs and the daily ceiling in the HTTP layer. A user-supplied key bypasses free runs and the ceiling but never the caps, since a runaway loop on someone else key is still our bug.

nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)

nodes.norm_label: product non-goals (no image generation, no batch/api/integrations, no accounts beyond metering, no mobile, no own editor, no presets)
nodes.rationale: Stated so that nobody builds them in the six build days available; a per-client house style is the obvious second product, not the first.

nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.norm_label: hard step cap as a product parameter

nodes.norm_label: user-supplied openai key handling (bypasses admission, not per-run caps; never stored)

The password-style form field is cleared when the start response arrives and never reaches sessionStorage, reducer state, analytics or error messages.

nodes.label: Bounded frame window
nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)

nodes.label: Daily ceiling sized against concurrency, not one user
nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.norm_label: daily ceiling sized against concurrency, not one user
nodes.rationale: Twenty concurrent runs at about $3.50 spend roughly $70 in one ten-minute wave, so a ceiling near fifty dollars trips on the first wave and NFR-4 holds only on paper; the number is a day-4 decision informed by spike A2.

nodes.label: No unit tests of model behaviour
nodes.community_name: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.norm_label: no unit tests of model behaviour
nodes.rationale: The model is not deterministic, and pretending otherwise wastes days the project does not have.

nodes.rationale: The lever between about $3.50 and $14.50 per run: a byte-stable tool array frozen per run, a 1,024-token minimum prefix, a 30-minute TTL refreshed on reuse, and the implicit breakpoint at the last tool response.

nodes.community_name: FR-20: apply a typed mid-run correction without discarding completed work
nodes.rationale: Long-lived persistent connections rule out serverless; one environment deployed from main from day 0 with no staging, object storage, one small relational store for metering and waitlist, and the landing page on the same domain.

nodes.community_name: FR-20: apply a typed mid-run correction without discarding completed work
nodes.rationale: A run is a stateful conversation lasting minutes that holds a browser session and streams frames, so it cannot resume from nothing on a cold invocation.

nodes.norm_label: nfr-8: per-run observability (step count, token spend, outcome, failure reason)

nodes.label: RunLogRecord one-line completion log
nodes.rationale: Exactly one JSON object per terminal run; the instruction is truncated to 200 characters, and frames and API keys are not fields, so they cannot be serialized accidentally.

nodes.label: RunRegistry background event pump with sixty-minute terminal retention
nodes.norm_label: runregistry background event pump with sixty-minute terminal retention
nodes.rationale: The pump stores ordered history, keeps a snapshot and broadcasts without depending on a connected page, so browser disconnects cannot pause a run. Terminal metadata is retained sixty minutes for launch-day reconnects but is not user history, and releaseSecrets() runs in finally on every terminal path.

nodes.label: Per-run structured log line
nodes.rationale: Run id, step count, cap hit, tokens in and out, cost, duration, outcome and failure reason, written at completion; frames are not logged, instructions are truncated, keys never appear.

nodes.norm_label: photopea licence question (answered: automated and commercial use permitted)
nodes.rationale: What remains is commercial rather than legal: free embedding shows advertisements, and removing them needs a Distributor account from 60 euros a month.

nodes.label: Risk: the scripting escape hatch
nodes.rationale: Scripting the retouching decisions rather than loading and exporting would let any model do the job; holding that line is a discipline problem, not a technical one.

nodes.label: ag-psd fallback
nodes.rationale: Writes layered PSDs from Node with no browser; a strictly worse product with nothing to watch or steer and no model leverage. The floor, not a plan: choosing it means the launch copy stops claiming computer use.

nodes.label: Browser provider shortlist (Browserbase, Anchor, Hyperbrowser, Steel)
nodes.norm_label: browser provider shortlist (browserbase, anchor, hyperbrowser, steel)
nodes.rationale: All expose a live-view iframe and a CDP endpoint from one session-create call; Steel Launch is disqualified at that tier because its fifteen-minute cap equals the run ceiling, and Anchor is noted for human handoff in a later version.

nodes.label: Browserbase
nodes.rationale: Default choice: the cheapest entry tier covering twenty concurrent runs, with a six-hour session length nowhere near binding.

nodes.label: Editor adapter
nodes.rationale: The only component that knows which editor is driven; everything else sees Contract 1. Its one design rule is the scripted vs driven split.

nodes.label: Embedded Photopea driven by the user (fallback product)
nodes.norm_label: embedded photopea driven by the user (fallback product)
nodes.rationale: A cross-origin iframe gives the parent page no pixels, and the agent input is pixels, so embedding only works for a weaker product where the agent writes scripts rather than looking.

nodes.label: Hosted Chrome session over CDP
nodes.rationale: One per run with Photopea loaded; needs CDP access, sessions of at least twenty minutes, concurrency for NFR-4 on the entry tier, and a live view.

nodes.label: Indirect prompt injection risk
nodes.rationale: The system card estimates an 8.5% attack success rate, and a confirmation policy barely moved unauthorised transactions (6.8%) or exfiltration (4.3%); asking the agent to confirm is not a control, making the bad action impossible is.

nodes.label: Machine-local cache overflow above 15 requests per minute
nodes.norm_label: machine-local cache overflow above 15 requests per minute
nodes.rationale: Twenty concurrent runs exceed the threshold in total; whether it counts per cached prefix or across the organisation is unknown and decides which cost row launch day lands in.

nodes.label: Photopea
nodes.rationale: Chosen because PSD is its native in-memory model, so it can emit a real layered file; it needs no account, key or contract, can be framed from any origin, and its terms permit any use.

nodes.label: Photopea Action Manager stub (stringIDToTypeID lookup table)
nodes.norm_label: photopea action manager stub (stringidtotypeid lookup table)
nodes.rationale: Closes the usual Photoshop escape hatch of dropping to action descriptors, so the judgement work is not scriptable even if wanted.

nodes.label: Photopea Distributor account
nodes.rationale: Free embedding shows ads in the product and the demo recording; removal costs from EUR 60 for 30 days at 1,000 frame-loads, has a signup lead time, and is bought on day 0.

nodes.label: Spike A4: OpenAI tier vs NFR-4
nodes.norm_label: spike a4: openai tier vs nfr-4
nodes.rationale: Day 0, one hour; the other spike that can still change the plan.

nodes.label: Spike B0: buy the Distributor account and re-read the terms
nodes.norm_label: spike b0: buy the distributor account and re-read the terms
nodes.rationale: No longer gates anything: the licence question is answered, and what remains is a purchase with a signup lead time.

nodes.label: Run admission order (body ceiling, instruction, image, visitor identity, meter, upload, RunHandle)
nodes.norm_label: run admission order (body ceiling, instruction, image, visitor identity, meter, upload, runhandle)
nodes.rationale: Ordered to avoid paid work for invalid or refused requests: an admission or persistence failure never starts a browser session, and a failure after quota reservation releases the reservation.

nodes.label: Required FREE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD (no default daily ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Startup fails when the value is absent or invalid; the team-approved value and its concurrency arithmetic must be committed to the TRD before issue 29 closes.

nodes.label: Export-then-destroy session disposal
nodes.rationale: The session holds the only copy of the work, so FR-12 and FR-13 are unsatisfiable if teardown wins; export first on every path, best-effort on error, and never let a failed export block the teardown that stops the bill.

nodes.label: Fifteen-minute run ceiling
nodes.rationale: The single ceiling everywhere: the sixty-minute WebSocket lifetime is an outer bound and the twenty-minute provider session is margin. Sizing the step cap against sixty would make it four times too large.

nodes.label: OpenAI tier rate limit as the concurrency ceiling
nodes.norm_label: openai tier rate limit as the concurrency ceiling
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 allows 500 requests and 500,000 tokens per minute with image tokens counted, which twenty runs exhaust before the server notices; raising the tier has a lead time, so it is checked on day 0.

nodes.label: Scripted vs GUI-driven split (the line that protects the premise)
nodes.norm_label: scripted vs gui-driven split (the line that protects the premise)
nodes.rationale: Loading, layer naming, export and viewport are scripted; selecting the subject, masks, adjustments and judging the edit are driven through the GUI. Scripting the retouching decisions would let any model do the job.

nodes.label: Self-hosted Playwright remote Chrome (rejected)
nodes.rationale: A watchable, interruptible remote Chrome is weeks of work: arbitrating human takeover and keeping raw CDP (Runtime.evaluate, cookies) away from the user browser. If no provider works, the product changes instead.

nodes.label: Structural agent security controls
nodes.rationale: The browser reaches only the editor origin by network allow-list, the session holds no credentials, the instruction and image are untrusted input, and sessions are destroyed after every run.

nodes.label: Unattended-run system prompt
nodes.rationale: Astra is documented as tentative about when to stop and as over-obeying instruction files, so the prompt says the run is unattended and carries no decorative prohibitions; the user instruction is a separate untrusted message.

nodes.label: Five-state pure client reducer (landing, input, running, result, error)
nodes.norm_label: five-state pure client reducer (landing, input, running, result, error)
nodes.rationale: State changes never navigate, and the reducer receives only validated API payloads, making reconnect, cap, cancellation, correction and failure behavior deterministic in tests.

nodes.label: Issue template chooser config (blank issues disabled)
nodes.norm_label: issue template chooser config (blank issues disabled)
nodes.rationale: Blank issues are disabled so that every issue starts from a template, and every template pre-fills a Conventional Commits type in the title.

nodes.label: Conventional lint workflow
nodes.rationale: Rules come from commitlint.config.mjs, so this check and the local .husky/commit-msg hook can never disagree.

nodes.label: Issue title lint workflow
nodes.rationale: GitHub cannot reject an issue at creation time, so an invalid title is labelled invalid-title, answered with a comment explaining the format when opened, and the check fails; the label clears once the title passes.

nodes.label: .husky/commit-msg hook
nodes.rationale: Blocks a commit whose message is not conventional, using the same commitlint rule set as the workflows.

nodes.label: Conventional commit types (build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test)
nodes.norm_label: conventional commit types (build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test)

nodes.label: Conventional Commits
nodes.rationale: Used for commit subjects, issue titles and pull request titles alike, so one glance at any of the three tells you what kind of change it is. Format: <type>[optional scope]: <description>, where the scope is an optional noun naming the part of the codebase touched and the description is imperative, lower case, with no trailing period.

nodes.label: Feature request issue form
nodes.rationale: Also the starting point for issues that are neither bug nor feature; the author changes the title type and the enhancement label to match.

nodes.label: Pull request template
nodes.rationale: Enforces nothing; it reminds the author of the title format, atomic commits, breaking-change marking and bun run lint.

nodes.label: Branch naming (<type>/<short-description>)
nodes.rationale: Reuses the commit types but is not machine-checked; it is a courtesy to whoever reads the branch list.

nodes.label: Breaking change marker (! and BREAKING CHANGE footer)
nodes.norm_label: breaking change marker (! and breaking change footer)
nodes.rationale: A breaking change takes a ! before the colon and explains itself in the body or in a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

nodes.label: gh pr create --fill-first
nodes.rationale: --fill takes the title from the branch name on a branch with more than one commit, which the title check rejects. --fill-first takes it from the first commit, which may not describe the whole branch, so pass --title when it does not.

nodes.label: Pass untrusted titles through the environment
nodes.norm_label: pass untrusted titles through the environment
nodes.rationale: The title is untrusted input, so it is passed through an environment variable rather than interpolated into the shell command.

nodes.label: Three product properties: editable output, visible work, steerable work
nodes.norm_label: three product properties: editable output, visible work, steerable work
nodes.rationale: Ordered by importance: the editable output is the product, visible operation is both the trust mechanism and the demo, and mid-run steering works like correcting a junior retoucher.

nodes.label: Async tool calling (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Dead: an orchestration ergonomics win that a job queue replicates and the user cannot feel.

nodes.label: Computer use (primitive)
nodes.rationale: The highest-leverage primitive and the best silent GIF; desktop hosting, not computer use, made Round 1 unshippable.

nodes.label: Computer use x mid-turn steering (Round 9)
nodes.rationale: Crossing the two surviving primitives passes the Swap Test on both axes at once; the desktop scope gate falls away once the target is web-based professional software.

nodes.label: Hosted-browser computer use (Round 2)
nodes.rationale: Removes the desktop VM fleet, but pointed at services it lands in crowded startup categories; the lesson is to point it at software instead.

nodes.label: Mid-turn steering (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Passes visibly because elsewhere changing your mind means cancel and re-prompt; it needs a generation long enough to interrupt and an artifact visible enough to see it going wrong.

nodes.label: Million-token single-pass context (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Clears the Swap Test only for inconsistency tasks: retrieval needs a query, and a contradiction has none.

nodes.label: Persisted reasoning and notes (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Dead: Astra has no cross-conversation memory, so persistence built on top of it works on any model.

nodes.label: Programmatic tool calling and orchestration (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Dead: a cost and latency optimisation; batch work that does pass does so for whole-corpus reasoning, not loop-writing.

nodes.norm_label: steerable financial model built in sheets

nodes.label: Idea shortlist scoring
nodes.rationale: Layerhand scores 27 with the highest ceiling and the shakiest floor (execution 3); a zero on leverage or execution would disqualify.

nodes.label: WebMCP
nodes.rationale: Dead by design: an open standard that decouples the page from the model scores zero on model leverage; worth it only as a surface attached to an Astra-only capability.

nodes.label: Inferred judging rubric (WebMCP Challenge criteria)
nodes.rationale: OpenAI published no judging criteria, so ideas are scored on the four equally weighted WebMCP Challenge criteria plus launch legibility and showcase-ability, an inference from the nearest comparable contest.

nodes.label: Ideation kill gates (scope, crowding)
nodes.rationale: Scope (five build days, no hosted desktop VM fleet) and crowding (existing startup categories, prior hackathon winners) removed ideas that passed the Swap Test.

nodes.label: Swap Test

nodes.label: Brushed metal cap
nodes.rationale: The weakest stretch of the subject outline: its top edge (luma about 170) is only about 36 levels from the paper above it (about 206), against 150-170 levels at the glass sides, so a subject selection is most likely to clip or bleed there. Lit from the left, it has a bright vertical specular band (luma about 245) left of centre and a shaded right half (50-95).

nodes.label: Cast shadow
nodes.rationale: Lit from the left, the bottle throws a soft shadow back and to the right across the floor (about x 900-1300, y 700-830), about 60 levels darker than the paper. Its core (about RGB 155,139,139) is cooler than the warm paper (about 210,199,185), likely light filtered through the cobalt glass, so a kept shadow must keep that tint. It is what 'keep the product shadow' protects when the background is removed.

nodes.label: Cobalt glass bottle
nodes.rationale: The subject to select and mask, centred in the frame: the glass spans about x 639-894 and y 310-820, and with the cap the subject runs from y 148 to about 840. Its sides contrast strongly with the paper (glass luma 40-60 against about 215). The translucent glass lightens and desaturates from the shoulder (luma 13-27) to the lower body (38-54) and turns nearly neutral at the heavy base where it meets the floor. It has no label, so an instruction to leave the label unchanged has nothing to protect here.

nodes.label: Dust specks
nodes.rationale: At least a dozen distinct dark spots on the floor of the sweep, the clearest near (1254, 825), (177, 871) and (40, 840), up to about 145 levels darker than the surrounding paper. Each is only a few pixels across, and smaller still once Photopea fits the photograph into the agent's 1440x900 view, which makes them easy for the agent to miss.

nodes.label: Glass reflections
nodes.rationale: A bright window-like highlight on the upper-left shoulder (about x 690-750, y 378-412) and fainter vertical streaks down the left third of the body (around x 690-730, luma 64-107 against 19-45 for the glass), consistent with light from the left. They are what an instruction to clean the reflections targets, but they also model the bottle's roundness, so removing them outright would flatten it.

nodes.label: Paper crease
nodes.rationale: A vertical crease right of the bottle and the strongest line in the background: mean horizontal gradient at x 1118-1136 is 1.9-2.2 against 0.93 elsewhere, and it is visible from top to bottom. A defect to heal on a kept background, or one a cut-out discards.

nodes.label: Paper sweep backdrop
nodes.rationale: What any background edit acts on. The paper is dull rather than white (median image luma 202), warm (red above blue by 20-35 levels), and unevenly lit, falling from about RGB 232,223,210 at the left edge to about 196,181,163 at the right, so removing, evening or neutralising it is visible work.

nodes.rationale: Output is condensed to save tokens while keeping every signal, so treat it as the complete result, run commands normally and batch related commands to avoid extra turns.

nodes.label: graphify-labs/graphify skill collection
nodes.rationale: Builds a knowledge graph of the repository in graphify-out/ and answers questions from it, so agents read a scoped subgraph instead of raw files.

nodes.norm_label: run bun run graph after modifying code
nodes.rationale: Keeps the graph current; runs graphify update . (AST-only, no API calls) then formats what it rewrote. Nothing does this automatically: the pre-commit hook no longer refreshes the graph.

nodes.label: Query the graph before reading source
nodes.norm_label: query the graph before reading source
nodes.rationale: graphify query, path and explain return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output; the wiki index serves broad navigation and GRAPH_REPORT.md only broad architecture review.

nodes.norm_label: refresh doc and concept nodes with /graphify --update
nodes.rationale: The AST pass leaves doc and concept nodes alone; refreshing those is the /graphify --update skill, which spends API budget. Never delete graphify-out/ first: graphify update . merges into the tracked graph.json, and rebuilding from an empty directory drops every semantic node.

nodes.norm_label: local hook setup (bun install, then uv tool install graphifyy)

nodes.norm_label: bun 1.4.2 runtime pin (lockfile version 2, frozen installs)

nodes.label: Surgical Changes
nodes.rationale: Touch only what you must and clean up only your own mess; every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

nodes.label: Atomic commits
nodes.rationale: One reason to change per commit, and every commit builds on its own; a subject that needs the word 'and' is two commits.

nodes.label: Conventional issue and pull request titles
nodes.norm_label: conventional issue and pull request titles
nodes.rationale: An issue describes the change as though committing it. Neither title becomes a commit subject, because rebase merges land the commits as written and discard the pull request title; the title is linted anyway because the pull request list, the notification and the reviewer see it first.

nodes.label: Rebase merge, never squash
nodes.rationale: Rebase is the only merge method, so commits land exactly as written and the atomic history survives where a squash would discard it. The branch is deleted after the merge.

nodes.label: Server-side repository setup (gh api merge settings)
nodes.norm_label: server-side repository setup (gh api merge settings)
nodes.rationale: Applied once through gh api by someone with admin on the repository: allow only rebase merges (squash and merge commits off), allow auto-merge, and delete branches on merge.

nodes.label: Single feat/launch-application branch, squash-merged by the coordinator
nodes.norm_label: single feat/launch-application branch, squash-merged by the coordinator
nodes.rationale: One isolated branch and pull request spanning several issues, commits atomic by behavior. The user authorized squash for this branch, an exception to the repository's rebase-only rule; merging follows independent diff review, a clean verification run and green checks, and a failing check, breaking contract change or unresolved security finding blocks it.

nodes.label: Stream-per-directory repository layout
nodes.rationale: One directory per stream so day-to-day work rarely collides; src/agent and src/editor meet only at Contract 1, src/server and src/agent only at Contract 2; existing conventions are not relaxed for the deadline.

nodes.label: Photopea postMessage protocol
nodes.rationale: A String is executed as a script, an ArrayBuffer is opened as a file (sidestepping CORS for URL loads), and an export arrives as an ArrayBuffer followed by "done" with no filename, MIME type or correlation id; startup configuration rides in the URL hash; export is saveToOE("psd").

nodes.label: Photopea known traps
nodes.rationale: Trap 1 and the Action Manager stub were confirmed by reading the shipped bundle; traps 2 to 6 (ES3 dialect, poisoned interpreter needing a reload, silent no-ops verified by reading state back, text layers needing two seconds, slow boot) are third-party recon until spike B1 confirms them.

nodes.label: Spike B1: verify the image-in, PSD-out round trip
nodes.norm_label: spike b1: verify the image-in, psd-out round trip
nodes.rationale: Day 0, half a day; confirms or strikes out each unverified Photopea trap.

nodes.label: Unique app.echoToOE sentinel per scripted call
nodes.norm_label: unique app.echotooe sentinel per scripted call
nodes.rationale: "done" is not a reliable terminator because some operations emit their own mid-script, so a naive wait desynchronises; a sentinel timeout means reload the frame, not retry.

nodes.label: Reusable Photopea bridge boot
nodes.rationale: From the September 14 review: concurrent boot calls share one readiness wait, a successful boot is cached and a failed one permits a fresh host, cleanup messages cannot satisfy a retry, and commandTimeoutMs bounds each message wait. The review also added header-field validation before navigation and applied the transport viewport to injected pages.

nodes.label: Pre-warmed editor sessions
nodes.rationale: About two seconds of boot plus a five-second first round trip overruns the five-second NFR-3 budget, so warming the session before the button is load-bearing and the first thing to measure.

nodes.label: obra/superpowers skill collection
nodes.rationale: Process skills, all 14: brainstorming, planning, test-driven development, debugging, verification, code review, and parallel agents.

nodes.label: Goal-Driven Execution
nodes.rationale: Turn tasks into verifiable goals and loop until verified; strong success criteria allow independent looping while weak ones need constant clarification.

nodes.label: Fenced code blocks with a declared language
nodes.norm_label: fenced code blocks with a declared language
nodes.rationale: Indented blocks cannot name a language, have ambiguous boundaries and are harder to find in Code Search. Declare the language so neither the highlighter nor the next editor must guess, escape newlines in copyable shell snippets, and indent blocks nested in lists.

nodes.label: [TOC] directive after the introduction
nodes.rationale: Use it unless all content is above the fold. Placement matters for screen readers and keyboard users, because [TOC] inserts the table of contents into the DOM wherever the directive appears.

nodes.label: Capitalization of titles and headings
nodes.rationale: Defers to the capitalization guidance of the Google Developer Documentation Style Guide.

nodes.label: Simplicity First
nodes.rationale: Minimum code that solves the problem and nothing speculative: no unrequested features, single-use abstractions, unrequested configurability or error handling for impossible scenarios.

nodes.label: Think Before Coding
nodes.rationale: Don't assume, don't hide confusion, surface tradeoffs: state assumptions, present competing interpretations, push back when a simpler approach exists, and stop to ask when something is unclear.
